title: Hope remains beside a goodbye

captions.physics: Supporting each other through recognised gestures
captions.emotions: Feeling the end of a stage

meaning: Your customs can sustain hope after a stage ends when saying goodbye retains a meaning of its own.
text: Another continuation does not cancel what has to be left behind. In the physical position of Anahata, the Hierophant expresses care through a shared custom or recognised sign of involvement. The Star in energy brings a wish to sustain hope and leave possibility beyond today’s ending. Death in emotions describes experiencing the close of a familiar stage. Tenderness can matter especially when both meanings coexist: the former stage really has ended, and life is not exhausted by it. Involvement helps avoid choosing between compulsory optimism and complete refusal to look beyond what is over.

Suppose classes you attended together for a long time are finishing. Instead of immediately searching for a replacement, you preserve the customary meeting after the last lesson. **Hope can support saying goodbye without hurrying it.** You can remember people, the route and the first awkward attempts. Familiar time together remains available although the shared stage has ended. Support need not require choosing another activity immediately; it leaves room to want something again after the former experience finds its place within your history.

The difficulty is working too hard to show how much good remains ahead. Regret looks insufficiently grateful for hope and begins being hidden. The shared custom survives but stops holding a real encounter. Warmth remains when support can be received while the loss of the familiar is acknowledged, without turning those responses into competing correct attitudes towards change.
